---
title: "Sources & methodology"
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

`swelections` combines official election information across source files,
election years, formats and geographic levels. Its two main official sources
are the Swedish Election Authority and Statistics Sweden (SCB).
The Swedish Election Authority is responsible for planning and coordinating the
implementation of elections. Statistics Sweden is responsible for official
election statistics.
The package uses data from both.

## Construction and validation

The legally established final result and official election protocols define the
final election outcome. The package combines detailed Election Authority files
with relevant Statistics Sweden tables and preserved historical sources, keeping their
definitions and coverage explicit. Statistics Sweden's official election statistics are also
used for validation and supplementation where relevant. Historical exports are
checked rather than assumed to be error-free.

Where a primary file is unavailable, preserved supplementary material, including
files derived from Statistics Sweden and Swedish National Data Service (SND) collections, may support
a documented reconstruction. Such supplements are identified and checked against
available official results; they are not presented as the missing original file.

Checks include vote totals, ballots cast, eligible voters, geographic aggregation,
seat allocations and reported candidate/list totals. They depend on what the
source reports and which counting stage it describes.

For original data and complementary resources beyond the package, see
[Other data resources](accessing-data.html#other-data-resources).

## Differences between sources

When sources disagree, the package checks whether they describe the same
election event, counting stage, geography and population. Other explanations
include category definitions, source versions, corrections and source errors.

Where the evidence establishes the correct value, the choice and reasoning are
recorded. Otherwise, the unresolved difference or aggregate is retained and
documented. Raw sources are not changed to force agreement, and votes are not
allocated to parties, candidates or districts without supporting evidence.
The [2002 reconciliation record](https://github.com/richardohrvall/swelections/blob/main/development/FINAL_RESULT_RECONCILIATION_2002.md)
and [EU 2009 completeness record](https://github.com/richardohrvall/swelections/blob/main/development/COMPLETENESS_EU_2009.md)
provide detailed examples.

## Canonical data

Canonical data are versioned Parquet files published with a `swelections` data
release. They provide a stable and reproducible data basis for the corresponding
package version and can be used without access to the underlying raw source
files. `canonical`, `remote` and `local` describe how data are obtained, not
different degrees of official status or quality. See
[Accessing the data](accessing-data.html) for source selection and direct file
access.

## Missing values and categories

A missing value, a verified zero and a value that is not applicable are different
states. Unsupported values remain `NA`, rather than being filled with zero.
Boolean properties use logical values, with separate applicability information
where needed. Missing electorate counts are not invented to calculate turnout.

Canonical data and English output use English technical categories. Swedish
interfaces translate categories and column names; proper names and literal
source identifiers retain their source spelling. `detail = "full"` adds source
information to the default `"standard"` output without changing shared values.

## Candidacies, candidates and mandate holders

`candidacies()` describes election-specific candidacies and ballot-list entries.
It can contain multiple list entries for the same candidate.
`candidates()` provides one row per candidate within the relevant election and
party, with additional candidate-level information where available. The resulting
data do not provide a longitudinal link between the same person across elections.

Candidate numbers have source-specific meanings. In older sources,
including 2006, rows can identify separate source observations rather than unique
people; equal names or numbers are not used to infer person identity.

`preference_votes()` returns reported candidate preference-vote observations at
the supported geographic or list level. Missing names or list-position links do
not erase reported votes. Alternative geographic and list views are not
additional votes to be added together.

`elected()` describes the final election outcome and `substitutes()` its reported
elected-member–substitute relationships. These are distinct from subsequent
mandate holding. `mandate_history()`, `members_at()` and `vacant_seats_at()` describe
holder and vacancy intervals over the same population of allocated mandates.
They do not describe attendance or temporary substitute service at meetings.

Re-elections are separate events within a continuing mandate period. Effective
post-re-election seat compositions retain the origins of their components.
See [Coverage](coverage.html) for the periods and events supported.

## Preliminary and final counting

The preliminary count begins at polling stations on election night and
continues with the collection/Wednesday count of late-arriving advance votes
and votes from abroad. Only parties expected to win seats are reported
separately at this stage; other parties may be grouped together. Personal votes
are not counted. Collection votes are reported in collection districts rather
than ordinary voting districts, to protect ballot secrecy.

The county administrative boards conduct the final count, checking votes and
counting every party's votes and personal votes. It starts on Monday after
election day, while the preliminary collection count takes place on Wednesday;
the processes therefore overlap. `preliminary` and `final` are different
counting stages, not complementary parts to add together. See the Election
Authority's [English explanation](https://www.val.se/english/the-swedish-electoral-system/preliminary-and-final-election-results)
and [Swedish guide](https://www.val.se/det-svenska-valsystemet/rostrakning-och-mandatfordelning/preliminar-rostrakning),
and [Understanding Swedish elections](understanding-elections.html#collection-districts)
for the geographic context. Missing preliminary snapshots are not completed
with final figures.

## Totals and geographic levels

Result tables often have one row per party. Eligible-voter counts, ballots cast
and other totals for the area can therefore appear on every party row. Summing
those repeated values across parties would count the same total more than once.

Geographic levels also overlap: voting districts belong to municipalities,
which belong to larger areas. Choose the level your analysis concerns rather
than adding the same population from several levels.

## Historical geography

The package retains the geographic divisions reported by each source.
Constituencies, voting districts and administrative units can change over time;
the same code or name does not necessarily identify exactly the same area in
different elections. See
[Understanding Swedish elections](understanding-elections.html#historical-comparability).
Better comparability through harmonisation of historical geographies is a
long-term development goal, not a completed feature.

## The 2003 euro referendum

`yes`, `no` and `blank` are reported voting options in the 2003 euro referendum.
They are categories, not Boolean values. Blank votes are separate from invalid
ballots. This structure is specific to that referendum and should not be
generalised to other elections.

## Code license and source data

The package code uses the MIT license. Source data retain their provenance
and the relevant publisher terms; see the
[Election Authority's open-data information](https://www.val.se/valresultat-och-statistik/statistik-och-data/om-var-oppna-data)
and [Statistics Sweden's open-data information](https://www.scb.se/en/services/open-data-api/).
These are separate from the package's code license.
